descriptor.scene: One anonymous traveler is the moving subject: seen from the side at mid-distance, a wiry traveler with a pack and a machete strides along a jungle trail from right to left, mid-swing through a hanging vine, eyes fixed ahead on the trail. Directly behind the traveler, an arm's length off the trail on the right half of the frame, stands the camouflaged elevator exactly as its locked camouflaged plate paints it: the cylindrical car wrapped in living vines and leaf-shadow, doors shut, glass dim, its silver ribbon lost among the lianas above. The traveler does not see it and never will. The joke and the ache of the picture is the arm's length between them. Keep the lower right calm ferns.
descriptor._caption: There is one way up. Elevators stand in the jungle, silver threads running from the forest floor to the island, and every one of them is camouflaged. You can cut a trail past one at arm's length and never know.
